_about: The free-placed level objects, shared by the game (level_data.gd, level_geometry.gd, grid_nav.gd) and the level editor. Sizes are metres. on_cell: what an object sitting square on a cell does to it ('wall' = counts as a wall for nav / lighting but no solid block is built; 'open' = punches a walkable opening through a wall). blocks_nav: when placed off-centre, the monster can't path across its span. A new structural type needs a builder in level_geometry.gd _build_objects(); the editor draws unknown types as a plain slab. A type with a 'model' key is instead a decorative clutter prop: level_geometry.gd's generic _build_props() instances that FBX/GLB and builds a PBR material from 'textures' (albedo/normal/roughness/metallic/emissive), no per-type builder needed. 'scatter': true marks it eligible for the level editor's random SCATTER PROPS tool. 'scale' on these objects (0.5-4.0, same field as thin_wall/arch width) is reused as a uniform size multiplier. Their 'elev' param is how far (metres) the model's lowest point is lifted off the floor. A model with no 'textures' keeps the materials in its own file (a .glb); 'glow' then sets how bright its emissive parts are. 'model_scale' is the size the model is built at (1 = as the file has it), so one file can be several types of different sizes; an object's 'scale' multiplies it. 'mount': 'wall' is a prop that hangs on a wall, back at its origin and front along the arrow: the level editor's 3D view puts it on the wall face you point at. Walls come in plan shapes ('shape': 'slab' straight, 'corner' an L, 'arc' a curve round the object's origin, 'pillar' / 'column' free-standing), built by level_geometry.gd _build_shaped_walls() / _build_column() from the same centre line level_data.gd shape_path() gives the nav. 'params' lists the per-object fields a type has beyond position / rotation / scale, with their defaults; the level editor's inspector shows exactly those (thick: metres, height: metres with 0 = up to the ceiling and anything under 1.8 m seen over, arc: degrees, depth: cells, event / text / once / delay / duration: a trigger's). 'max_scale' raises the 4-cell cap on scale, 'align': false stops the editor turning a piece to fit the wall it lands on. A 'zone' shape is an event trigger (props/event_trigger.gd), its 'events' the choices of what it runs. 'category' (walls, openings, events, props) is the level editor panel the type is listed in. 'draw_line': true lets the editor draw the piece as a line (click, drag to its end; Shift chains the next one on). 'stairs': true is a stairwell (props/stairs.gd): it stands square on two cells, the one it is on and the next along its arrow, and joins this floor to the next one up / down wherever that floor has a stairwell on the same cells. 'choices' lists the values a text param may take (value -> what it does); the inspector shows them as a drop-down. 'ranges' gives a numeric param its inspector row ([min, max, step, suffix, tip]) when no other type has one for that key. 'default_scale' is the width a type's first piece is placed at. More shapes: 'spline' (a wall along its 'points', object-space cells, smoothed through them; 'draw_spline': true lets the editor draw it point by point), 'platform' (a raised floor slab: 'depth' cells along the arrow by 'scale' across, its top 'elev' metres up), 'flight' (straight stairs climbing 'rise' metres along the arrow over 'depth' cells from 'elev'), 'spiral' (stairs wound round a column, 'scale' cells across), 'window' (a wall-mounted window onto a fake sky that throws sunlight in; props/window.gd) and 'water' (a water surface 'level' metres over the floor over a 'depth' by 'scale' box; props/water_body.gd). Platforms, flights and spirals are built by props/vertical_pieces.gd.

thin_wall.label: Thin wall
thin_wall.help: A slim partition. Thickness and Height in the inspector (Height 0 = up to the ceiling)

arch.label: Arch
arch.help: A round-topped opening. Square on a wall cell it punches through the wall; anywhere else it is a wall of its own with the arch in it, its sides reaching out to meet the walls beside it (within a cell and a half)

door.label: Door
door.help: A framed wood door set in its own thin wall; opens as you approach

squeeze_gap.label: Squeeze gap
squeeze_gap.help: A very tight slit through a wall (the Backrooms 'in between the walls' squeeze). Put it square on a wall cell: the wall closes round it and leaves a gap you turn sideways to pass. Gap = the opening width in metres

stairs_up.label: Stairs up
stairs_up.help: A stairwell from this floor to the one above: a boxed-in switchback stair two cells long, its doorway on the cell behind the arrow. The same stairwell is put on the floor above (which is made if the level has none). On a stairwell that is already here, it carries that one on up another floor

style.carpet: The level's own wallpaper and carpet
style.concrete: A bare concrete service stair with a painted steel rail

light.on: A tube lamp over every landing
light.off: No light at all: bring a torch

stairs_down.label: Stairs down
stairs_down.help: A stairwell from this floor to the one below: the same stair as Stairs up, with its other end put on the floor below (which is made if the level has none). On a stairwell that is already here, it carries that one on down another floor

style.carpet: The level's own wallpaper and carpet
style.concrete: A bare concrete service stair with a painted steel rail

light.on: A tube lamp over every landing
light.off: No light at all: bring a torch

half_wall.label: Half wall
half_wall.help: A waist-high partition: office cubicles, a counter, a railing along a drop. You see over it, you can't walk through it

wall_corner.label: Corner wall
wall_corner.help: An L of two walls meeting at the origin, each leg Width cells long: one along the facing arrow, one to its right. Put the origin on a cell corner to run the legs along cell edges

wall_curve.label: Curved wall
wall_curve.help: A wall bent round a circle centred on the origin: Width is the circle's diameter in cells, Arc how much of it is built, centred on the facing arrow. 90 rounds off a corner; 300-360 makes a round room (leave a gap to get in)

pillar.label: Square pillar
pillar.help: A free-standing wallpapered pillar, Thickness metres on a side. Rows of them make a pillar hall; square on a cell, that cell's tube light moves off it

column.label: Round column
column.help: A plastered round column, Thickness metres across

wall_spline.label: Spline wall
wall_spline.help: A wall laid along any curve you draw: click to drop its points, then Enter, a double click or a right click to finish it (Backspace takes the last point back, Esc drops it). Smooth bends it round through the points, Closed joins its ends into a loop (a round or bean-shaped room). Select it and drag its squares to move the points. Its tiles follow the curve without stretching

platform.label: Raised floor
platform.help: A floor slab held up off the ground: a mezzanine, a balcony, a landing, a walkway over the water. Width across the arrow and Depth along it (cells); Off floor is the height of its top (m). Edge: what runs round it (chrome pool rails, a tiled parapet, or nothing); a gap is left wherever a stair arrives at its height. Posts holds it up on square legs. Reach it with Stairs (straight) or Spiral stairs whose top is at the same height

edge.chrome: Chrome pool rails along every open edge
edge.parapet: A waist-high tiled parapet along every open edge
edge.none: Bare edges: nothing stops a fall

surface.tile: The level's tiled wall material (the pool rooms' white tiles)

slab: how thick the slab is, top to underside

stair_flight.label: Stairs (straight)
stair_flight.help: A straight flight of solid steps climbing the way the arrow points: Width across it, Depth = how far it runs (cells), Off floor = where its foot stands (m: 0 on the floor, or the top of a raised floor), Rise = how high it climbs (m). Rise 9 m (a storey: the default) takes it up through the ceiling onto the floor above: the ceiling opens over it and the floor above gets a hole for it to come up through (the floor above must have open floor there). Less goes onto a raised floor. No steeper than about 40 degrees (the status line warns). Railing: chrome pool rails on both sides, one side, or none

railing.both: A chrome rail on each side

surface.tile: The level's tiled wall material (the pool rooms' white tiles)

rise: how high it climbs from its foot. 9 m (a storey) takes it up through the ceiling onto the floor above

stair_spiral.label: Spiral stairs
stair_spiral.help: A spiral stair wound round a tiled column: Width = its diameter (cells), Off floor = where it starts (m), Rise = how high it climbs (m), Sweep = how far round it goes (360 = one full turn), Core = the column's width (m). Turn: which way it climbs. The first step is at the arrow. Rise 9 m (the default) takes it up through the ceiling to the floor above, which gets a hole for it; less: put a Raised floor at its top for a landing. Rail: a chrome rail round its open side

surface.tile: The level's tiled wall material (the pool rooms' white tiles)

sweep: how far round it climbs: 360 is one full turn

pool.label: Pool
pool.help: A pool sunk into the floor, any shape: click its corners round (Enter, a double click or a right click closes it; a click with no shape drawn drops a 3 x 2 cell one). Shallow and Deep are the depths at the end the arrow comes from and the end it points to (the floor slopes between), Lip how far under the rim the water lies. A tiled basin, a rounded coping, steps down into the shallow end and a chrome ladder at the deep end. You swim in it (Space up, crouch to dive, push into the side to climb out). Reshape it: drag its squares, Shift+click its edge to add a corner, Ctrl+click a corner to take it out

tint.teal: Pool water: clear, going teal-green with depth
tint.murky: Old green water you can't see far into

shallow: how deep it is at the end the arrow comes from
deep: how deep it is at the end the arrow points to
lip: how far under the rim the water lies

window.label: Window
window.help: A window onto a bright outside that isn't there: the sky and the sun through the glass, and real sunlight thrown into the room through its panes (their shadows land on the floor). Put it on a wall face, its arrow pointing into the room. Width along the wall (cells), Height and Off floor (the sill, m), Frame (panes, a round porthole, an arched top, a floor-to-ceiling panorama), Panes (glazing bars), Sun (how much light it throws), Sun angle (how high the sun stands), Sky (the light's colour)

frame.pane: A square-cut window with glazing bars
frame.porthole: A round porthole (Width is its diameter)
frame.arched: Glazing bars under a round arched top
frame.panorama: A wall of glass from the sill nearly to the ceiling

sky.noon: A white midday sun in a pale blue sky
sky.overcast: A bright, flat, shadowless white sky

panes: how many lights across (the glazing bars between them)
sun: how strong the sunlight it throws into the room is
sun_angle: how high the sun stands: low throws a long patch across the floor

water.label: Water
water.help: Standing water: Width across the arrow, Depth along it (cells), Level = how high its surface stands over the floor (m), from ankle deep to over your head. It reflects the room, throws rippling light (caustics) on the walls and ceiling round it and the floor under it, tints and fogs with depth, slows you as you wade, splashes underfoot and closes over your head. Lay it wall to wall; it is only a surface, so where it ends in the open its edge is a sheer glassy side

tint.teal: Pool water: clear, going teal-green with depth
tint.murky: Old green water you can't see far into

level: how high the surface stands over the floor (1.6 m and up closes over your head)

trigger.label: Event trigger
trigger.help: An invisible box that runs an event when the player walks into it: Width across the arrow, Depth along it (cells). Pick the Event, an optional Text caption, a Delay, and whether it only ever fires Once

events.message: Camcorder TV message with black box at top of screen
events.text: Camcorder TV message with black box at top of screen
events.alert: T.S.R.A. terminal alert card with CRT glow, typewriter text, chime, and 5s life bar
events.lights_out: The tubes over the box die for Duration seconds, then re-strike
events.flicker: The tubes over the box stutter
events.silence: The ambience drains away for Duration seconds; only the hum is left
events.drone: A low drone swells for Duration seconds
events.spawn_bacteria: Summon Bacteria monster near the trigger
events.spawn_mimic: Spawn a Mimic anomaly near the trigger
events.spawn_mannequin: Activate / warp Mannequin into the room
events.camera_shake: Camera shake / trauma when stepping in
events.hallucination: Breathing and whispers close behind you
events.wallKnock: Director event: knocking inside a wall behind you
events.breathBehind: Director event: something breathing on your neck
events.preacherWhisper: Director event: a preacher's voice down a corridor
events.powerCut: Director event: the whole floor's power fails for a minute
events.redAlert: Director event: every light drops to slow pulsing emergency red; something walks the halls
events.emergencyPulse: Director event: every light beats red like a heart, quickens, skips and fails
events.lightsOut: Director event: the grid fails in stages, then something walks up to you in the dark
events.oneLamp: Director event: everything dark but the tube over you; something breathes under the next one
events.deadAir: Director event: you are deafened; ringing, a warped picture, two knocks behind you
events.machineVoice: Director event: an old crushed text-to-speech voice reads a disturbing line
events.context_voice: Context voice: while the player is in the box, whenever something new happens to them (lights die, torch off or low, something close, a teammate dies, they freeze or run...) the machine voice says a line about it. Duration = seconds between lines; Once = only one line
events.ghostRoster: Director event: a researcher who isn't anyone joins the expedition (sometimes it's you)
events.humRises: Director event: the fluorescent hum climbs until it hurts, then every sound stops
events.partyWall: Director event: a party behind the drywall; go to it and it stops dead, then one knock
events.phoneRing: Director event: a phone rings down the halls; it stops before you reach it, then rings behind you
events.houndPacing: Director event: footsteps far off behind the walls keep pace with you; stop and they stop, then one step nearer
events.run: Director event: black, then red lights rush down the hall toward you with something running under them
events.itHeardYou: Director event: DO NOT SPEAK. It listens to the microphone; say anything and the lights die and something comes
events.sayYourName: Director event: the machine voice slowly says the player's callsign, twice
events.answerBack: Director event: two knocks; say something and the wall knocks back once for every word
events.yourOwnVoice: Director event: the player's own voice, saying something they said earlier, from down the hall
events.doorbell: Director event: a doorbell far off, then nearer
events.lookTogether: Director event: an advisory (do not look up... we will look together); the head tilts back by itself
events.soundsToAvoid: Director event: a card lists three sounds to avoid; a little later you hear the third
events.countdown: Director event: a timer counts down from 60; at zero nothing happens; then it counts up

prop_explosive_barrel.label: Explosive barrel
prop_explosive_barrel.help: A rusty red hazard drum. Purely decorative clutter

prop_water_barrel.label: Water barrel
prop_water_barrel.help: A blue plastic drum. Purely decorative clutter

prop_gas_can.label: Gas can
prop_gas_can.help: A small jerry can. Purely decorative clutter

prop_gas_cylinder.label: Gas cylinder
prop_gas_cylinder.help: A tall pressurised tank. Purely decorative clutter

prop_cable_drum.label: Cable drum
prop_cable_drum.help: A big wooden cable spool. Purely decorative clutter

prop_car_jack.label: Car jack
prop_car_jack.help: A hydraulic floor jack. Purely decorative clutter

prop_electrical_box.label: Electrical box
prop_electrical_box.help: A wall-mount breaker box. Purely decorative clutter

prop_electrical_box2.label: Electrical box (b)
prop_electrical_box2.help: A second breaker box variant. Purely decorative clutter

prop_pallet_truck.label: Pallet truck
prop_pallet_truck.help: A manual pallet jack. Purely decorative clutter

prop_platform_trolley.label: Platform trolley
prop_platform_trolley.help: A flatbed warehouse trolley. Purely decorative clutter

prop_work_light.label: Work light
prop_work_light.help: A T.S.R.A floor work lamp. Casts real light: the research teams set these up to light their areas

prop_work_light2.label: Work light (b)
prop_work_light2.help: A second T.S.R.A work lamp variant with two flood heads. Casts real light toward the ground like research lights

prop_exit_sign.label: Exit sign (small)
prop_exit_sign.help: A lit green running-man EXIT sign for a wall, 31 cm wide (Width is its size multiplier). Its back sits flat on the wall and the arrow points out into the room. In the 3D view (F4) point at a wall and click: it goes on that wall, at that height

prop_exit_sign_medium.label: Exit sign (medium)
prop_exit_sign_medium.help: The EXIT sign at 2.5 times its size: 78 cm wide, 48 cm high, read from down a corridor. For a wall, like the small one

prop_exit_sign_big.label: Exit sign (big)
prop_exit_sign_big.help: The EXIT sign blown up 6 times: 1.9 m wide, 1.15 m high, a wall of green light. Width takes it up to 4 times that. For a wall, like the small one

prop_stop_sign.label: Stop sign
prop_stop_sign.help: A red STOP sign on a metal pole, 2.4 m tall. Purely decorative

prop_stop_sign_worn.label: Stop sign (worn)
prop_stop_sign_worn.help: A weathered STOP sign on a pole, 2.4 m tall. Purely decorative

prop_stop_sign_tyro.label: Stop sign (plain)
prop_stop_sign_tyro.help: A plain STOP sign on a pole, 2.4 m tall. Purely decorative
